firewallLog.note: per-protocol filterlog columns: srcport/dstport are emitted only for port-bearing protocols (tcp/udp) and tcpflags only for tcp, so an icmp/igmp/esp-only poll window omits the keys. Verified live 2026-07-13 (icmp/igmp rows carry neither). Box/traffic state, not a version prune

firmware.note: firmware/status serves a minimal envelope until a check has run since boot, then a state-dependent superset (~26 top-level keys, we model 12); the unmodelled remainder is exempted wholesale so canary results do not depend on when the box last ran a check. downgrade_packages/reinstall_packages are now modelled as count gauges (#237). The 26.7 full-inventory keys (all_packages/all_sets) remain a #227 opportunity

firmwareInfo.note: release changelog metadata, the full package inventory (~380 KB payload) and the product detail object; not modelled. First validated 2026-07-13 — before the ForceAttemptHTTP2 fix this endpoint always failed to probe over HTTP/1.1, so these keys never surfaced

idsStatus.note: GUI widget metadata on service-status responses; never consumed

idsQueryAlerts.note: bootgrid query metadata (active filters, the eve.json origin) served alongside the alert rows; not modelled

idsSettings.note: cross-generation IPS-mode representation: <= 26.1 carries the boolean ids.general.ips, 26.7 replaced it with the ids.general.mode pcap/netmap/divert selector. The exporter reads whichever is present. Prune ids.general.ips when 26.1 leaves the support window; ids.general.mode.* covers the reverse (mode absent on <= 26.1)

hasyncVersion.note: present only for some HA peer states; box has no HA peer

healthCheck.note: legacy pre-26.1.11 health shape (top-level per-subsystem objects + metadata.<Subsystem>); 26.1.11+ serves only metadata.system plus metadata.subsystems, which the tolerant reader prefers. Prune when 26.1.10 and older leave the support window

interfaces.note: capture timestamp of the interface statistics snapshot; not modelled

interfacesOverview.note: LAGG (laggproto/lagghash/laggstatistics/laggport) and bridge (members) fields are hardware/config-dependent — only served by a row that is itself a lagg(4)/bridge(4) interface. Verified empirically 2026-07-13: absent on both the live prod box (no lagg, no bridge configured) and the 26.7-devel VM (virtio-only, no lagg/bridge module loaded). rows[].sfp.* already covers every sfp key uniformly (including the DOM-only temperature/voltage/lane_*_rx_power/lane_*_tx_bias keys) via the map wildcard, so no separate exemption is needed there — a copper RJ45 SFP's identity-only keys (verified live: UBNT UF-RJ45-1G) already satisfy the wildcard (#214)

ipsecSad.note: the NAT-T marker is emitted by list_sad.py only when the SA is NAT-traversed (setkey reports a NAT src/dst); absent as a key otherwise. Box state (whether a peer sits behind NAT), not a version prune. #213

netbirdStatus.note: netbird CLI status --json (client/status.OutputOverview, github.com/netbirdio/netbird) node identity/config/session fields the exporter does not model — an #211 opportunity if a future metric needs them. Separately (not expressible as an exemption here): the daemon-down state serves a bare `[]` instead of this object (verified live 2026-07-13); a canary run that catches the box in that state will report a top-level Mismatch for this endpoint — that is the documented daemon-down fallback (see opnsense/netbird.go), not drift

protocolStatistics.note: cross-generation tcp counters. ecn ce/ect0/ect1-packets: renamed received-* in 26.1.11, legacy kept for ≤ 26.1.10 — prune when 26.1 leaves the support window. received-acks-for-unsent-data: split in 26.7 into received-acks-for-data-{not-yet-sent,never-been-sent,being-too-old}, which are now modelled as a presence-gated counter (#237); the legacy aggregate stays decoded-only (never fed a metric). syncache receivd-cookies/sent-cookies (upstream's typo included): moved to statistics.tcp.syncookies.* in 26.7, now modelled as a presence-gated counter (#237); decoded-only, no metric impact.
